import { type AgUiChat, defineChat } from "./static/vendor/agents-web-components.bundle.js";

defineChat();
const chat = document.querySelector("ag-ui-chat") as AgUiChat;
chat.routeMap = [{ id: "home", path: "/", title: "Home" }];
chat.navigate = (path) => history.pushState(null, "", path);

No node_modules and no @types package are involved; pnpm build type-checks exactly this kind of host (scripts/bundle-types.mjs) and fails if the file ever reaches for a package. A host that copies only the .bundle.js (as django-admin-agent does, for templates with no TypeScript) is unaffected.

docs.title: Markdown rendering
docs.text:
Assistant bubbles render sanitized markdown/HTML via marked (GitHub-flavoured, single-newline line breaks) piped through DOMPurify. User messages stay literal text. The allowlist permits emphasis, code, lists, quotes, headings, links, tables, and — when allowImages is set — images; links are hardened with target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"; iframe/style/scripting are excluded, as are every data-* and aria-* attribute and every class but a code fence's language-* hint, so model output cannot dress itself up as the component's own approval or tool-call chrome. The exported helper renderMarkdown(text) does this standalone. marked and dompurify are runtime dependencies.

An animated 3-dot "thinking" indicator (role="status", with an aria-label) appears before the first token and between tool rounds, honouring prefers-reduced-motion. It has no public API.

docs.title: Incoming-text animations
docs.text:
The data-text-animation attribute controls how a fully-received assistant message reveals: none (default) / fade (a CSS fade) / word (JS word-by-word via the internal wrapWords reveal). It honours prefers-reduced-motion (collapsing to instant).

<ag-ui-chat endpoint="/agent/" data-text-animation="word"></ag-ui-chat>

docs.title: Follow-up suggestions
docs.text:
The agent can offer the next question, not just answer this one. Registered skill chips are static and host-configured, so they can say "summarize this" but never "want me to update the shipping address too?" after a tool has run.

The server pushes an ACTIVITY_SNAPSHOT under the suggestions type — with django-ag-ui, suggestions_activity([...]). The component draws each prompt as a chip; clicking one sends it as the user's message, exactly as if they had typed it.

{ "activityType": "suggestions",
  "content": { "prompts": ["Update the shipping address too"] } }

Chips are content. They ride the same activity envelope as charts, so they persist and a reload puts them back, and a set pushed under an id already on screen replaces that row rather than adding a second one.

At most 4 prompts of 120 characters each — MAX_SUGGESTIONS and MAX_SUGGESTION_CHARS, both exported. The server-side helper raises past those bounds while this side silently drops: that asymmetry is deliberate, since the producer can report the problem and the client cannot.

Nothing to enable. A suggestions activity from a server that pushes one is drawn; an activity_type this component does not know is ignored, which is what the open field is for.

docs.title: Localizing the timestamps
docs.text:
There is no Intl anywhere in this component. The relative timestamps in the thread drawer and checkpoint panel ("5m ago", "2d ago") are deliberately locale-neutral: a component that guessed a locale would disagree with the page it is embedded in, and being wrong in a second language is worse than being neutral in one.

That is a good default and a bad requirement, so it is replaceable:

const rtf = new Intl.RelativeTimeFormat("de", { numeric: "auto" });
chat.formatRelativeTime = (ts) =>
  rtf.format(Math.round((ts - Date.now()) / 60000), "minute");

relativeTime is exported too, for a host that wants to build on the built-in rather than replace it.

docs.title: Message actions: copy, retry, feedback
docs.text:
Every finished assistant message carries a small row of actions beneath it — a sibling of the bubble, never a child, so the buttons never join the message's own text.

  • Retry re-asks the question. History is truncated to the most recent user message inclusive and the run repeats, so the agent answers what it was asked rather than being told its last answer was wrong. After chat.run, Retry answers for the action instead: it asks for a refused one again, unchanged, and is not offered once the action's run started (see Starting a run with forwarded props).
  • Copy puts the message's text on the clipboard, and says so on the button. A refused clipboard permission is reported there too, rather than thrown.
  • Thumbs up / down fire ag-ui-feedback (wired below) and store nothing. Off unless you ask for them — data-message-actions="copy,retry,feedback". Without a listener the buttons still latch, so a reader is told a rating was taken while nothing recorded it.

Retry sits on the last answer only. Re-running an older turn is branching, and for a page-driving agent editing a past turn is not neutral — those turns clicked buttons, and re-running turn 3 does not un-save what turn 5 saved.

Note

A retried turn re-runs its tools. The previous attempt already did what it did, and this does not undo it. Confirmation still applies, so a destructive tool asks again — unless the user waived it for this session with Always allow.

A failed run gets the same row, with Retry and Copy and no rating: error text is what people paste into a bug report, but "the connection dropped" is not a statement about answer quality and mixing it into feedback makes that signal say less. This is why a dropped connection is still rendered as an error rather than demoted to a run notice — a notice "never settles, takes no action, and carries no controls", and a failure with a way back needs one.

The row can be trimmed, or removed, with data-message-actions — a comma list of the actions to keep, or ="false" for none at all:

<!-- copy only: nothing here listens for a rating, and the surface forbids re-runs -->
<ag-ui-chat endpoint="/agent/" data-message-actions="copy"></ag-ui-chat>

The default is copy,retry. Those two work with nothing wired; the rating pair needs a listener, so it is asked for rather than assumed.

docs.title: What Copy puts on the clipboard
docs.text:
Both flavours of the message: text/plain for anywhere, and text/html for a target that understands it. A table therefore pastes into a spreadsheet as columns and into a document as a table.

The plain flavour is serialised structurally rather than read off textContent, which is the obvious source and loses everything: it concatenates descendants with no separator, so a table arrives as one unbroken run of cells with the headers welded to the first row. Rows are tab separated because that is what a spreadsheet splits on; list items keep their bullets and numbers; a code block keeps its own whitespace.

Both flavours are taken from a copy of the message with the component's own buttons removed. The code blocks' copy buttons live inside their pre, so they are descendants of the message: before this, copying an answer containing a code block copied the word Copy along with it.

A host that drives its own bar gets the same by passing html alongside text to attachMessageActions; with text alone the clipboard gets plain text only, exactly as before.

docs.title: Sizing and theming the row
docs.text:
The controls are icon-only, so the whole box is the target. It is sized from --ag-ui-action-size, with a floor rather than a fixed height so the compact density cannot shrink it below the 24px that keeps it reliably tappable.

Each control draws its own label on hover and on keyboard focus. That is not the title attribute repeated: a title never appears on focus, so an icon-only button is unnamed for anyone tabbing to it. On a touch device, where there is no hover to reveal it and it would sit over the answer, it is not drawn at all.

ag-ui-chat {
  --ag-ui-action-size: 28px;        /* the control box; floors at 24px */
  --ag-ui-action-icon-size: 15px;   /* the mark inside it */
  --ag-ui-tooltip-bg: #1f2430;
  --ag-ui-tooltip-fg: #f5f6fa;
}

To swap a mark for your own, style its part — message-action-icon-copy and its siblings. A slot would be the better channel and cannot be used: these repeat once per message, and a named slot can only be filled once.

It is per-action rather than one switch because the three disappear for different reasons. Thumbs are only useful to a host listening for ag-ui-feedback, and two buttons that lead nowhere are worse than none. Retry re-runs the agent, which a constrained surface may not permit. Copy is the one nobody objects to — and with a single switch, dropping either of the others would have cost it too. Nothing survives, and no row is built at all: an empty row still takes its margin and still announces itself as a group of actions.

retryLastTurn() is public, for a host driving its own message UI.

await chat.retryLastTurn(); // false when there is nothing to ask again, a run is in flight, or a restore is loading

docs.title: Storing a rating
docs.text:
ag-ui-feedback names the message that was rated, so a host can file the rating against it rather than against its text — two answers can read the same, and nothing about the text survives a reload:

Field Type What it is messageId string The AG-UI id of the rated assistant message: the id it streamed under (TEXT_MESSAGE_START / TEXT_MESSAGE_END), or the stored message's id when it was restored from history. A restored answer whose store returned no id offers no rating pair, since a rating has to name a message. threadId string The conversation it belongs to: the element's thread when the message was drawn. runId string, optional The run that streamed it, as that run's RUN_STARTED named it. Text a sub-agent streams through the parent run carries the parent's runId. Absent on a restored message — an AG-UI message carries no run id, so there is none to give and the key is left out rather than guessed. content string The message's text, as rendered. rating "up" | "down" Which button. 
chat.setAttribute("data-message-actions", "copy,retry,feedback");
chat.addEventListener("ag-ui-feedback", (e) => {
  const { messageId, threadId, runId, rating } = e.detail;
  // Keyed by message: rating the same answer again replaces the earlier rating.
  fetch(`/api/threads/${threadId}/ratings/${messageId}/`, {
    method: "PUT",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify({ rating, ...(runId === undefined ? {} : { runId }) }),
  });
});

Note

A restored message is named by whatever id the conversation store returns for it. The built-in browser store saves the conversation as it streamed, so there a message keeps its id across a reload. With data-threads-url or a conversationStore of your own, the conversation comes back from your server, and a message keeps its id only if the server persists the ids it streamed: one that stores the conversation under fresh ids makes a rating made live and a rating made after a reload name the same answer by two different ids. Live, the id is always the one on the wire.

docs.title: Sources an answer cites
docs.text:
When the model says which sources back its answer (pydantic-ai's TextPart.citations, carried by django-ag-ui 0.90.0 and later), the answer gets a collapsed Sources (n) list under its text, above the action row. Nothing to opt in to: an answer with no citations looks as before.

The list reads the assistant message's metadata.citations: live from the TEXT_MESSAGE_END that closes it (which @ag-ui/client 1.0 also folds onto the message it saves), and after a reload from the stored message the thread endpoint returns. Each entry is pydantic-ai's Citation in its JSON form:

Key Drawn as sources One line per source. A web source is a link to its url (only http and https become links; anything else is shown as text), named by its title or else the URL. A document source is its title, else its document_id, else the string citationDocument. Each of excerpts is quoted under it. anchor {kind: "content", start, end}: the cited range of the answer, quoted. {kind: "marker", ...}: the model's own marker such as [1], shown as code. null: sources only.

start and end count UTF-16 code units into the message's own content, so content.slice(start, end) is the range. The range is quoted rather than highlighted in the bubble, because the offsets index the markdown source and the rendered text is shifted by its syntax. An anchor that does not fit the text is dropped and its sources kept; a citation with no usable source is dropped. Titles, URLs and excerpts go in as text, never as HTML.

Live and reloaded copies can differ. Text on both sides of a file part streams as two messages, each with its own citations, and is stored as one message joined by a newline under a fresh id, its citations indexing the joined text. So the answer draws as two bubbles live and one after a reload, each list read against its own text. A rating given live names the streamed ids; after a reload, the stored one. A split around reasoning or a provider compaction is stored under the ids it streamed, so it draws and rates the same either way.

Copy and a rating's content leave the list out. Style it through the citations part, or the strings citations (token {count}) and citationDocument.

docs.title: The model a fallback answer came from
docs.text:
When a run's first model fails and a fallback model answers (pydantic-ai's ModelFallback, or django-spec-agents' build_model_fallback), the answer gets a muted Answered by openai:gpt-5 line under its text, above its sources. Nothing to opt in to: an answer the request's first model gave shows no line.

The line reads the assistant message's metadata, as django-ag-ui 0.91.0 and later writes it: live from TEXT_MESSAGE_END, and after a reload from the stored message. It is drawn only when model_fallback is true and model_id is a non-empty string, and it names model_id as the server sent it (the id the model was configured by).

Copy and a rating's content leave the line out. Style it through the answered-by-model part, or reword it with the string answeredByModel (token {model}).

docs.title: Quoting a selection
docs.text:
Select any text in the transcript and a small Quote offer floats beside it. Taking it drops the selection into the composer as a markdown blockquote and leaves the caret on a fresh line under it — a quotation is how a question narrows to one part of an answer, so nothing is sent until you say what you are asking.

Quoting appends, after whatever is already typed, so a second quotation is a second thing being asked about rather than a replacement for the first. Long selections are capped at 500 characters: select-all-then-quote is a gesture the transcript already answers, and pasting the whole conversation back costs tokens to say nothing.

Set data-quote-selection="false" to turn the offer off. The quote-selection part styles it.

docs.title: The half that matters: selection in your page
docs.text:
The transcript is the easy half. A chat mounted beside a table, a diff or a report is sitting in the surface the user actually works in — and that selection is one no hosted chat can reach.

offerQuoteInPage() extends the same select-then-offer gesture to the whole page. It is opt-in, because it listens on your document:

const stop = chat.offerQuoteInPage();       // the whole page
chat.offerQuoteInPage(document.querySelector("#report")); // or one region

For a deliberate trigger instead of a selection, quote(text) is the seam underneath:

// "Ask about this row" — a button on each row of your own table.
row.querySelector(".ask").addEventListener("click", () => {
  chat.quote(row.innerText);
});

quote() never sends — pair it with sendMessage() if you want a one-click "explain this" that skips the composer entirely.

Do not write the four-line version of offerQuoteInPage(). A mouseup listener that quotes every settled selection appends to the composer on every drag the user made to read, to copy, or to fix a typo — and it cannot tell a selection in your prose from one inside the user's own half-typed <input>, because Chrome reports a field's internal selection through document.getSelection() as an ordinary range over the field's wrapper. The text reads back perfectly and nothing about the range says where it came from; the only signal is document.activeElement. That guard, plus skipping the widget's own transcript, plus retiring a fixed-position affordance on scroll, is what the method is for.

Reading a selection out of a shadow tree takes care too. Engines disagree about what document.getSelection() reports for a selection made inside a shadow root: WebKit rescopes the endpoints to the host element, so you get the whole widget and none of the words, while Chromium hands back the shadow nodes directly. getComposedRanges settles it, and this component uses it where it exists. quotableSelection(container, roots) is exported if you have the same problem in your own component.

docs.title: Moving from @artooi/ag-ui-web-component
docs.text:
The old package is replaced, not upgraded: the tags, events, parts, slots and --ag-ui-* custom properties keep their names, so markup and stylesheets carry over untouched. What changes is the package, how the element is defined, and a handful of removals.

Install the new package and remove the old one. Never keep both on a page: each defines the <ag-ui-chat> tag, and the second to load cannot claim it.

npm uninstall @artooi/ag-ui-web-component
npm install @artooi/agents-web-components

A vendored bundle is renamed too: dist/agents-web-components.bundle.js replaces dist/ag-ui-web-component.bundle.js.

Define the element. defineAgUiChat is now defineChat, and it lives on the ./chat entry. Importing the package still registers nothing, so the call stays explicit:

// before
import { defineAgUiChat } from "@artooi/ag-ui-web-component";
defineAgUiChat();

// after
import { defineChat } from "@artooi/agents-web-components/chat";
defineChat();

The bundle exports it too (import { defineChat } from "@artooi/agents-web-components/bundle"). defineChat() does nothing when AgUiChat already holds the tag, and throws, naming the tag, when another class holds it, which is how a second copy of the element shows itself.

The first deploy forgets what the browser stored. Every storage key now starts with agents-web-components instead of ag-ui-chat, and nothing migrates the old keys. The first page load after the move starts from the defaults: the open thread, the collapsed state, the panel size, the launcher and dock position and the theme are gone once, and so is the drawer's list of threads, unless data-threads-url is set, in which case the server still supplies it. A host that reads the old keys itself must read the new root.

Removed names. Each is gone; most have a replacement that behaves the same:

Removed Use instead defineAgUiChat defineChat, from ./chat createStateHookTools, StateHook createPageStateTools, PageState the element's registerStateHook method registerPageState AgUiClient.annotatedMessages AgUiClient.messages the noResult string in UiStrings nothing: callNotFinished answers a call that never returned

A string table that still sets noResult stops type-checking; delete the entry.

Server-side rendering. The element extends HTMLElement and some helpers read the DOM, so evaluating the package in Node throws. Import it on the client only: from a client-side module, a dynamic import() behind a browser check, or your framework's client-only boundary. The package declares sideEffects: false, so an unused import is dropped, but that is a bundling property, not a promise that the modules load without a DOM.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Drop the element into your page and register the tools the agent may call:

<script type="module">
  import { fillField, clickElement, X_DESTRUCTIVE_KEY } from "@artooi/agents-web-components";
  import { defineChat } from "@artooi/agents-web-components/chat";

  // Register the <ag-ui-chat> Custom Element. An explicit call, not an import
  // side effect, so importing the package defines nothing. Idempotent; it throws
  // if another class already holds the tag (a second copy of the element).
  defineChat();

  const chat = document.querySelector("ag-ui-chat");

  // Extra request headers (e.g. CSRF), sent with every request the element makes.
  // For a credential that rotates, set chat.getHeaders instead - it is consulted
  // per request. See "Authenticating requests".
  chat.headers = { "X-CSRFToken": getCsrfToken() };

  // A non-destructive tool: fills a text field with a typing animation.
  chat.registerTool({
    name: "fill_field",
    description: "Fill a text input by id with a value.",
    parameters: {
      type: "object",
      properties: { field: { type: "string" }, value: { type: "string" } },
      required: ["field", "value"],
    },
    handler: async ({ field, value }) => {
      await fillField(document.getElementById(field), String(value));
      return "ok";
    },
  });

  // A destructive tool: x-destructive at the JSON-Schema root gates it behind
  // the inline confirmation card before the handler runs.
  chat.registerTool({
    name: "save_article",
    description: "Save the article. Destructive — asks for confirmation.",
    parameters: { type: "object", properties: {}, [X_DESTRUCTIVE_KEY]: true },
    handler: async () => {
      await clickElement(document.getElementById("save"));
      return "saved";
    },
  });
</script>

<ag-ui-chat endpoint="/agent/" title-text="Assistant"></ag-ui-chat>

Important

If nothing appears, check that defineChat() ran. Forgetting it looks like nothing at all. <ag-ui-chat> is then an unknown element, which every browser renders as an inline 0x0 box, in flow, with no console warning and no error — so the page looks finished and the chat is simply absent. There is nothing to search for.

A bare import "@artooi/agents-web-components" registers nothing, deliberately: registration is an explicit call so the package stays tree-shakeable.

customElements.get("ag-ui-chat") in a console answers it in one line. undefined means the call did not run.

That's the whole integration: an endpoint attribute pointing at your AG-UI server, optional headers, and the tools you want the agent to be able to invoke in the browser. If your API is on another origin, add credentials="include" too; see Authenticating requests.

docs.title: Attributes and properties
docs.text:
Attributes (set in HTML; the CSS-only ones are styling presets with no JS API):

Attribute Property Notes endpoint endpoint The AG-UI endpoint URL. Required to send: without it a send is refused with a console.error naming the missing attribute and a not-connected run notice in the transcript. Reflecting getter + setter. credentials credentials Cookie policy for every request the element makes: omit / same-origin / include. Unset means the browser default (same-origin), which sends no cookies cross-origin. See Authenticating requests. title-text — Header label; defaults to "Assistant". "auto" makes the header, the rail and the bar label follow the thread on screen (threadTitle), falling back to the strings table's title while it has none. Live: writing it after the element connects re-labels the header. See When each attribute is read. data-tool-display toolDisplay How tool calls are drawn: grouped (the default: a run's consecutive calls fold into one row) / inline / minimal / compact / full (per-call cards; full was the default before grouped). An unknown value reads as grouped. See Tool-call display modes. data-tool-group-display toolGroupDisplay How an opened step group draws its calls under grouped: full (the default) / compact / minimal / inline. Ignored under the four card modes. An absent or unknown value reads as full. See Choosing how a group draws its calls. data-text-animation — Incoming-text reveal: none (default) / fade / word. data-prompt-chips — Present (bare, or any value but "false") to surface skills as chips. data-slash-commands — Present (bare, or any value but "false") to enable the /-command palette. data-skills — Inline JSON skill catalog. A value that will not parse is ignored and reported on the console, rather than reading as an empty catalog. data-skills-url — URL of a JSON skill catalog (fetched with the element's headers and cookie policy). data-skill-editor-url — URL of django-ag-ui's skill editor endpoint (skills/editor/). Opts into the skill editor: a "Manage skills" row at the foot of the / palette under data-slash-commands, a header button with data-skill-editor-button, or openSkillEditor(). data-routines-url — URL of django-ag-ui's routines editor (routines/, from 0.86.0). Opts into routines: a Routines button in the header, a Make this a routine item in its More menu, openRoutines() and makeRoutine(). Read at connect time, like the other endpoint URLs. data-routine-minute-step 5 The minute step of the routine form's time field, a whole number from 1 to 30; anything else keeps 5. Read each time the form opens. A routine saved at a minute off the step still shows that minute. See The time and timezone fields. data-skill-editor-button absent With data-skill-editor-url, also puts a Skills button in the header. Off by default. On a narrow panel it moves into the header's More menu like the other optional controls. data-editors absent external hands the skill editor and routines to the page: the Skills and Routines buttons, Make this a routine and the palette's Manage skills fire ag-ui-open-editor instead of opening the view in the panel, for an editor element to answer. Read at each click. The methods still open the panel. data-tools-url — URL of a server tool-label catalog ([{ name, summary, description? }]), fetched with the element's headers and cookie policy; labels tool-call cards for server-side tools. user-key userKey Who the stored conversation belongs to — any string identifying the signed-in principal. Joins the storage namespace, and changing it purges what the previous principal left behind. Live (not connect-time): a logout is the host's to announce. See Who the stored conversation belongs to. user-name userName The signed-in user's display name, for the greeting an empty conversation shows under placement="page". Presentation only: unlike user-key it scopes nothing and is never sent. Absent or blank gives the nameless greeting. Live. data-threads-url — URL of a server thread index (django-ag-ui's ThreadsView, or any server that keeps to the threads contract); enables durable, cross-device chat history. data-detach-runs — Opt-in, read at each request. With data-threads-url, a run outlives its connection: a thread switch, New chat or the element leaving the page lets go of it instead of stopping it, opening a thread whose run is still going joins it, and Stop posts the thread's cancel/. Needs a django-ag-ui 0.82.0+ mount; see Runs that outlive their connection. Without data-threads-url it does nothing. data-poll-runs — Opt-in, live. With data-detach-runs and data-threads-url, the chat asks the open thread's run log every five seconds while idle and joins a run the server started there by itself (a child's report waking its parent, say), or restores the thread when that run parked on an approval, with no thread watch. Under data-thread-status the watch already does this; see Runs that outlive their connection. data-threads-cache — On by default. ="false" stops mirroring message bodies into sessionStorage when data-threads-url is set, for a deployment that put history on the server so transcripts stay off the client. Only meaningful alongside data-threads-url. data-runs-url — URL of a server run index (django-ag-ui's RunsView); reveals the header's Continue a run panel. See Resuming a run. data-attachments-url — URL of the file-upload endpoint (django-ag-ui's AttachmentsView); reveals the composer's paperclip picker, drag-and-drop, and paste. data-attachment-accept — <input accept> list for client-side type filtering (e.g. image/*,.pdf). The server stays authoritative. data-attachment-max-bytes — Client-side upload size cap in bytes (default 10 MiB; 0 disables). The server stays authoritative. data-transcribe-url — URL of the voice-transcription endpoint (django-ag-ui's TranscribeView); reveals the composer's mic button. See Voice input. data-theme-toggle — Boolean: show a built-in header light⇄dark toggle (persists per tab). Off by default. See Theme toggle. data-strings strings Partial JSON override of the UI string table (localization). The property wins key-by-key over the attribute; a value that will not parse is ignored and reported on the console. See Internationalization. data-icon-url — Header (and launcher) icon image URL. A slotted slot="icon" wins; see Header & launcher icon. data-launcher-icon-url — Icon image URL for the collapsed launcher only, when it should differ from the header's. Falls back to data-icon-url; a slotted slot="launcher" wins over both. data-unread-badge — On by default. ="false" hides the launcher's unread badge; the count and the ag-ui-unread event keep running. See Collapsing to the launcher. data-launcher-drag — On by default. ="false" leaves the widget wherever your CSS puts it. Otherwise the collapsed launcher can be dragged anywhere on screen (the panel opens into the clearest space) and the open panel can be dragged by its header. See Moving the launcher and Moving the panel. data-quote-selection — On by default. ="false" stops the transcript offering to quote a selection. quote() keeps working either way. See Quoting a selection. data-message-actions — Copy and retry by default; feedback is opt-in. A comma list of the actions a finished answer keeps: copy / retry / feedback (e.g. "copy,retry,feedback" to add the rating pair, which needs an ag-ui-feedback listener). ="false" removes the row entirely. See Message actions. data-max-tool-rounds — Upper bound on frontend tool-call → re-run rounds within one send (default 10; a value below 1 is ignored). Raise it for a page-driving agent whose turn takes many small steps. See The run loop. data-page-actions — Opt-in built-in page-action tools: a comma list of scroll / drag / chat (e.g. "scroll,drag"). See Page-action tools. data-side — For placement="sidebar": which edge it docks to, right (default) / left. Styling, and read by script for the side dockWidth and ag-ui-dock-width report. Live. data-collapse-icon — The header collapse control's mark: panel-close (a window with its docked pane and an arrow into the edge, mirrored on data-side="left") / chevron-up / chevron-down / chevron-left / chevron-right. Absent, or any other value, follows the placement: panel-close on sidebar (and side), chevron-down everywhere else. A host icon in slot="icon-collapse" wins over it. Live. data-answer-well — CSS-only boolean: box each assistant turn (its text, tool cards, and thinking) in one bordered "well". Off by default. See The answer well. collapsed collapsed Reflected boolean; collapses the widget to its launcher (a rail under placement="sidebar", the header bar under embedded). Persisted per tab. placement="page" has no collapsed state and ignores it. collapse-to — What the panel collapses to: auto (the default; absent or any other value reads the same) leaves every placement as it is, bar draws a strip along the bottom edge in place of the round launcher, none hides the collapsed widget so the host's own control brings it back. Under either, a corner panel still moves by its header and moveTo on a wide viewport, and remembers where it was dragged. Live. See Collapsing to a bottom bar. anchor anchor Under collapse-to="none", a selector for the host's element the panel rises from, right-aligned to it. The anchor property takes an element instead and wins over the attribute. Live. maximized maximized Reflected boolean; grows the open panel to its maximized size. Refused on page, full and embedded, at 600px or less, and while collapsed; a collapse leaves it. Not persisted. Live. anchor-side — Under collapse-to="none" with an anchor, which side of it the panel opens on: above, below, or auto (the default, and any other value), which takes the side with more room and re-decides on a window resize, never during a drag. Live. data-dragging — Written by the element, not by you. Stamped on whichever handle a gesture is currently using, so the styles can react and so the element knows not to re-place the widget under a drag in progress. Cleared on pointerup and on pointercancel. data-expand-corner — Written by the element, not by you. It stamps the corner a dragged or agent-moved panel opens from, so the collapse animation starts where the panel actually is. Listed because the element reads its own stamp back; setting it yourself is overwritten on the next move. data-greeting — CSS-only: off turns the greeting layout off under placement="page", where it is on by default. Any other value turns it on under placement="embedded". No other placement has it. data-empty — Written by the element, not by you. Present while the conversation has nothing in it, which is when the greeting shows. Public as a styling hook, so the chrome around a full-page chat can react to the same state, e.g. ag-ui-chat[data-empty] ~ .page-footer { display: none }. data-running — Written by the element, not by you. Present while an interaction is in flight, the same state that shows the Stop button (see the running property). Public as a styling hook, as data-empty is, so the chrome around the chat can react to it, e.g. ag-ui-chat[data-running] ~ .toolbar button { pointer-events: none }. data-threads-search — When the conversation list shows its search box: auto (absent, or any other value) from eight conversations, always over any list, never not at all. Live. See The conversation list. data-thread-status — Watch the conversation list for run status and unread: poll asks again every five seconds with the last ETag, stream follows the server's event stream (and polls when the server answers with JSON). Each list is handed on in ag-ui-threads-change. Needs a store with watchThreads, as data-threads-url gives. Live. See Thread status. data-small-viewport — off keeps the desktop layout at every width, opting out of the small-viewport override. Styling, and read by script for the width dockWidth reports on a phone. Live. Everything that override sets is a token you can re-state; its trigger is a media query, which is the one thing you cannot. data-paste-attach — When to turn a long text paste into an attachment instead of composer text: absent for the 5000-character default, off to never, or a positive number of characters. Only acts where data-attachments-url (or a custom uploadHandler) gives it somewhere to go. data-starters — JSON array of prompts offered on an empty transcript, e.g. '["Summarise this page"]'. Fallback content for slot="empty", so slotting your own replaces them. Shares the four-prompt and 120-character limits with the suggestion chips a run pushes. Read once at connect. data-start-open — Mount the panel open on a first visit. The corner placements otherwise rest at their launcher, the way every corner chat does; a stored choice wins over both. The placements that place themselves are unaffected. show-usage — Present (bare, or any value but "false") to draw a muted token-usage line under each finished turn, from the usage RUN_FINISHED carries (django-ag-ui's include_usage). Read when the turn settles. See When a run fails, and what it cost. theme — Styling: an optional theme name (quiet (default) / soft / ledger / classic, or a word of your own) and an optional scheme (light (default) / dark / auto), in any order, e.g. soft dark. Live: the header theme toggle's glyph follows a scheme written after connect. See Themes. density — CSS-only: comfortable (default) / compact. placement — CSS-only: floating (default) / sidebar / page / embedded / full. full fills the viewport at every width, inside the safe-area insets; the --ag-ui-inset, size and --ag-ui-panel-radius tokens still apply.

Each header control also takes its own icon slot — icon-history, icon-checkpoints, icon-new, icon-maximize, icon-collapse — with the built-in drawn glyph as the fallback, so a host can project a brand <img> or <svg> in its place. The built-in header marks are drawn at --ag-ui-glyph-size. The composer's glyphs work the same way: icon-send, icon-stop, icon-attach, icon-voice.

<ag-ui-chat endpoint="/agent/">
  <svg slot="icon-new" width="16" height="16"><!-- ... --></svg>
</ag-ui-chat>

The collapse control's built-in mark follows the placement, because a sidebar hides sideways into its edge rather than down: panel-close (a window with its docked pane and an arrow into the edge) on sidebar and side, mirrored for either on data-side="left", and chevron-down on floating, full, embedded and every other placement. data-collapse-icon picks one of the built-in marks outright, at any placement and live: panel-close, chevron-up, chevron-down, chevron-left or chevron-right; any other value reads as absent. panel-close always points into the edge the panel docks to, so it mirrors on a left docked panel whether chosen or defaulted; the chevrons do not turn. For a mark of your own, slot it into icon-collapse, which wins over the attribute and every placement:

<ag-ui-chat endpoint="/agent/" placement="floating" data-collapse-icon="chevron-right"></ag-ui-chat>
<ag-ui-chat endpoint="/agent/" placement="sidebar">
  <svg slot="icon-collapse" width="16" height="16"><!-- ... --></svg>
</ag-ui-chat>

docs.title: When each attribute is read
docs.text:
The element observes two groups of attributes, and they behave differently once it is in the DOM. Nothing outside those groups is observed: a CSS-only attribute (theme, density, data-answer-well, data-tool-group-display) is read by the stylesheet rather than by script, and endpoint, data-tool-display, data-text-animation, data-runs-url, data-page-actions, data-message-actions, data-max-tool-rounds, data-unread-badge, data-launcher-drag and data-quote-selection are re-read at each use, so a late write to any of those simply takes effect. The one attribute in neither camp is data-launcher-icon-url: it is read while the element connects, like the group below, but is not observed, so a late write is inert and says nothing.

Live attributes. Written at any time, before or after the element connects, and acted on either way: title-text, placement, collapse-to, anchor, anchor-side, maximized, data-side, data-small-viewport, data-threads-search, data-thread-status, data-poll-runs, credentials, user-key, user-name, data-tool-group-display, data-collapse-icon, theme.

Connect-time attributes. Read once, while the element connects, to decide what chrome exists at all — the tray, the mic, the skills menu, the header mark. Writing one afterwards has no effect; the element logs a console warning naming the attribute rather than failing silently, because the symptom is an affordance that never appears and that reads as a broken component. Set them before the element enters the DOM, or remove and re-insert it. See Framework hosts, where the boundary bites hardest. The list: data-attachments-url, data-attachment-accept, data-attachment-max-bytes, data-transcribe-url, data-threads-url, data-threads-cache, data-tools-url, data-skills-url, data-skill-editor-url, data-skill-editor-button, data-routines-url, data-skills, data-prompt-chips, data-slash-commands, data-theme-toggle, data-strings, data-icon-url.

What re-inserting costs: the chrome is built again from the attributes as they stand, a run in progress is cancelled, and the conversation is redrawn from its stored history — the same rebuild reload() performs, and the reason that method exists for a host that can only configure the element after the fact.

Properties (JS only, not attributes): headers, getHeaders, trustedOrigins, allowImages, autoConfirm, confirmPredicate, askUser, askUserRenderer, approvalRenderer, approveWithEdits, agentFactory, getTools, getContext, routeMap, navigate, getPageMap, autoInjectPageMap, getPlace, conversationStore, uploadHandler, transcribeHandler, navigationResult, skillContext, toolSummaries, formatToolPayload, formatRelativeTime, strings, resolvePageTarget, sharedState, anchor (an element, which wins over the attribute's selector), extraStyles (unstable), plus the read-only unread, unhandledActivityTypes, threadId, threadTitle, tabs, running, barHeight, dockWidth, uiStrings, colorScheme and locale, and the attribute mirrors endpoint / userKey / userName / toolDisplay / toolGroupDisplay / collapsed / maximized / credentials / detachRuns.

headers and getHeaders authenticate every request the element makes, not only the agent run; getHeaders is the one to use for a credential that rotates. See Authenticating requests.

allowImages (default false) re-enables <img> in rendered assistant markdown. It is off by default because a model-controlled image URL is fetched by the browser with no user interaction — a zero-click exfiltration channel for prompt-injected page data. Enable only when the content source is trusted.

toolSummaries is a Record<string, string> mapping tool name → a friendly card label, used when a tool has no x-summary in its own schema. Built-in and client tools should carry x-summary directly; this map is the seam for server-side tools (drf-mcp, the django-ag-ui @tool registry), whose schema never reaches the browser — e.g. chat.toolSummaries = { list_projects: "Search projects" }. Or point data-tools-url at a server catalog endpoint (django-ag-ui's tools/) and the labels are fetched automatically — per card, x-summary → an explicit toolSummaries entry → the fetched catalog → the raw name.

sharedState is AG-UI shared state, documented under the run loop; unread and unhandledActivityTypes are read-only counters, covered under the unread badge and finding out what arrived; threadId and running are covered under driving the conversation from your own chrome.

Code blocks in an agent's answer carry a copy button, revealed on hover or keyboard focus and styleable via the code-copy part. Override its labels with the copyCode / copied / copyFailed strings.

Methods: registerTool, registerPageState, registerActivityRenderer, registerContext, setSkills, refreshSkills, openSkillEditor, closeSkillEditor, openRoutines, makeRoutine, routineSeed, closeRoutines, sendMessage, run, attachFile, appendMessage, retryLastTurn, quote, offerQuoteInPage, enableCharts, newChat, setCollapsed, toggleCollapsed, setMaximized, toggleMaximized, describeSurface, moveTo, resetSize, toggleTheme, openThreads, closeThreads, switchThread, deleteThread, openTab, closeTab, openCheckpoints, closeCheckpoints, toggleCheckpoints, refreshPlace, request, tokenValues and reload.

request(url, init?) is fetch as the element authenticates: headers and getHeaders() under init.headers (which win per key), and credentials unless init names its own. A destination outside trustedOrigins is reported as the element's own requests are. It is the seam a separate entry such as ./mcp-apps reaches the host's routes through.

refreshSkills() fetches data-skills-url again, so the / palette lists a skill written elsewhere. routineSeed() is what Make this a routine would fill a form with: { prompt, name } from the conversation's user messages, or null before anything is said. An editor element bound to the chat calls both.

colorScheme is the scheme the panel is drawn in now ("light" or "dark"); a change of the theme attribute fires ag-ui-theme with { scheme }. locale is the nearest lang attribute, looked for past any shadow root the element is in, else the browser's language. tokenValues(names) returns the values the panel computes for the custom properties names (a colour resolved in the current scheme), leaving out any it does not declare. ./mcp-apps hands a view the theme through these three.

docs.title: Sending from your own UI
docs.text:
sendMessage(content, attachments?) sends as if the user had typed it — user bubble, ag-ui-submit event, run started. ag-ui-submit means a turn was sent, not that a run started: a Retry and a run continued from the checkpoint panel start runs without one. To know whether anything is running, read running or style on data-running. Use it for an "Ask about this order" button, a command palette, a prompt fired when your page mounts the chat, or a composer of your own replacing the built-in one.

It returns a Promise<boolean>. It resolves true once the turn has been handed to the agent and its run has settled, frontend-tool rounds included, and false when nothing was sent:

  • for an entirely empty message;
  • while a run, or a checkpoint continuation picked from the panel, is in flight. A continuation counts from the pick, and a send from the call rather than from when its run starts, so a sendMessage from an ag-ui-submit listener, or a second call in the same task, is refused rather than starting a second run;
  • with no endpoint set, which the transcript also says;
  • while a reload resumes a run a navigating tool interrupted. The resume counts from the moment the element asks its conversation store for the conversation, and it ends by starting that run, so a send then is refused, and the built-in Send queues behind the resumed answer;
  • when your own code that runs on the way to the request — an ag-ui-submit listener, the conversation store's save — stops it by starting a new chat or changing user-key. A getContext or getTools that does the same stops it too, but after the turn was handed over, so the call resolves true.

While the element restores a stored conversation, a send waits for it. Every restore — when the element connects, on reload(), when a thread is picked from the drawer, and when user-key changes from one principal to another — first asks the conversation store for the conversation, and with data-threads-url that is a request to your server. A sendMessage made in that time waits until the conversation is drawn, then sends with it: the bubble, the ag-ui-submit event and the request all come after the replay, later than the call by the length of the load. So a prompt fired on mount needs no timing of its own. If New chat, a thread switch, a change from one user-key to another or a reload() comes while it waits, the conversation it was addressed to is gone, so it is dropped and resolves false at once. The element leaving the page drops it too, but it resolves false only once the load answers or the element is inserted again. A first user-key on an anonymous conversation adopts that conversation rather than replacing it, so a send waiting then still goes out. A second sendMessage while one waits is refused. The built-in Send queues what is typed during the load ("Waiting to send"), and sends it after the conversation is drawn, behind a sendMessage that was waiting.

Unlike the built-in Send it does not queue, so your composer keeps what it tried to send, and it does not consult the attachment tray: what you pass is what is sent, so your composer stays in charge of its own state.

retryLastTurn() keeps the same rules, because it starts a run on the same conversation. It returns false while a run, a send, another Retry or a continuation is in flight, and while any restore of the stored conversation is still loading. It does not wait for the load as a send does: until the conversation is drawn there is nothing on screen to retry, and afterwards it would ask the previous visit's last question again. It counts from the call as a send does: until its run starts, a sendMessage or a second Retry is refused, the built-in Send queues, and a checkpoint pick is refused. It also returns false when your own code stops it before its run starts: a conversation store, or an activity or tool renderer it redraws through, that starts a new chat or changes user-key. A getContext or getTools that does the same stops it too, before anything is sent, but it runs after the Retry has handed its turn to the client, so the call resolves true. A store that throws from the Retry's save leaves the conversation as it was, and retryLastTurn() rejects with its error.

attachFile(file) queues a file into the tray exactly as the picker and drag-and-drop do, with the same validation and progress chip. It returns false when uploads are not configured (no data-attachments-url and no uploadHandler) — the only way to tell, since with no tray there is nothing to report through.

Uploading is asynchronous, so watch ag-ui-attachments for the result. Its detail carries { attachments, pending }: the durable refs of everything that has finished, and how many are still in flight. Send once pending is 0, or you will leave files behind.

chat.addEventListener("ag-ui-attachments", (e) => {
  const { attachments, pending } = e.detail;
  sendButton.disabled = pending > 0;
  sendButton.onclick = () => chat.sendMessage(input.value, attachments);
});
chat.attachFile(fileInput.files[0]);

docs.title: Starting a run with forwarded props
docs.text:
run({ forwardedProps, runId?, message? }) starts a run for an action the server reads from RunAgentInput.forwardedProps rather than from a typed turn, such as what the user picked on a surface an activity drew.

await chat.run({
  forwardedProps: { action: "approve", surface: "s1" },
  runId: actionRunId,
  message: { id: `${actionRunId}-turn`, content: "Approve the refund" },
});
  • Only the first request carries forwardedProps and runId. runId reaches the wire unchanged, so you can derive ids from it. The rounds a frontend tool or an approval starts afterwards send {} and a run id of their own, because a server that acts on the props would otherwise act again for every round. Under data-detach-runs every round's forwardedProps also carries detach: true, and the later rounds send that alone.
  • message is the turn the server stores, under your id. It is drawn as the user's bubble and announced by ag-ui-submit, as a sendMessage turn is, but it is not in the first request's messages, which would put it in the conversation twice. When that request's RUN_STARTED arrives, the turn joins the element's copy of the conversation, after the history that request posted and before the reply. From then on every request posts it, the follow-up rounds of the same run included, and the store saves it, so a reload draws it again. A run refused before RUN_STARTED keeps nothing. Without message, nothing is drawn or announced. A message with empty content is refused.
  • It refuses and waits as sendMessage does. It resolves false while a run, a send or a picked checkpoint's continuation is in flight, and with no endpoint. Behind a restore it waits, then runs. It resolves true once the run is handed to the client.
  • Retry asks for a refused action again, unchanged. When the first request is refused before RUN_STARTED, the failed bubble's Retry (and retryLastTurn()) sends the same forwardedProps, the same runId and no message in messages, and redraws the turn once rather than adding a second bubble. Once RUN_STARTED arrives the server holds the action, so Retry is withdrawn, from the earlier answer too, and retryLastTurn() resolves false without touching the conversation; so it does after a Stop. The next sendMessage or checkpoint continuation brings Retry back, and New chat, a thread switch or a reload forgets the action: a restored conversation's Retry re-asks its last user turn, the action's included, as a sent one.

docs.title: Adding to every run's context
docs.text:
registerContext(provider) adds entries to every run's context beside getContext rather than in place of it, and returns the function that removes them again:

const unregister = chat.registerContext(() => [
  { description: "open_surface", value: JSON.stringify(surface.state) },
]);
// later
unregister();

Each round's context is what getContext returns, then each registered provider's entries in registration order, then the place. Providers are read fresh for every round, a checkpoint continuation's included, and are filtered like getContext's while the place is withheld. Use it when a piece of your page has something to say for as long as it is on screen, without taking getContext over from whatever else set it.

A self-contained demo lives in demo/. Run make demo from a clean checkout: it installs, builds and serves the demo against a scripted AG-UI server on port 5173. Every feature has its own scenario page, grouped in the left nav; each page has the controls for that feature and Try buttons that send the prompts the scripted agent answers. The start page lists every prompt, and /page/ is the chat as a host's own full-page route.

docs.title: Charts
docs.text:
Markdown here goes through a narrow sanitiser and images are off by default — a model-controlled image URL is fetched with no user interaction, which turns prompt-injected page data into a zero-click exfiltration channel. So a chart does not arrive as markup. It arrives as data, and the component builds the SVG itself: the model chooses the numbers, the component chooses the DOM.

Off unless you ask for it, by either route or both:

const chat = document.querySelector("ag-ui-chat");
chat.enableCharts(["tool", "activity"]);

Order does not matter. Calling it after the element is on the page redraws any charts already in the restored history, so you do not have to reach the element before it connects — which you generally cannot.

Specs are bounded, and anything outside is dropped rather than half-drawn: at most 20,000 points and 2,000 labels, and every point a finite number no larger than 1e15. The first two keep a stored transcript from blocking the main thread on every reload; the last one keeps the value range finite, since scaling divides by it.

"tool" registers a render_chart tool the agent may call. The numbers are in its context, so it can talk about them; it costs one model round.

"activity" draws a chart the server pushes as an ACTIVITY_SNAPSHOT with activityType: "chart" (exported as CHART_ACTIVITY_TYPE). The data never reaches the model, there is no extra round, and this is the only route that can update a chart in place — the server repeats the same messageId to redraw it, or sends an ACTIVITY_DELTA to move one series as a computation advances.

Whether a pushed chart survives a reload depends on where the conversation is stored. A client-side store keeps activities, so it comes back. A server that stores the thread as the model's message history does not — a pushed chart is deliberately not in that history, which is the reason to push it. A chart the agent asked for survives either way, because its spec travels as the tool call's arguments and the component redraws from those without re-running anything.

A server that wants the pushed chart back opts in: django-ag-ui's AGUIServer(thread_activity_source=...) (a ThreadActivitySource) materialises each activity as an activity message in GET <id>/, and the component redraws it. The threads contract states the shape.

Either way the payload is the same shape:

{
  "kind": "bar",
  "title": "Signups this week",
  "labels": ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed"],
  "series": [{ "label": "new", "points": [12, 19, 9] }]
}

kind is one of bar, line, pie, scatter, stacked; anything else is drawn as a bar rather than refused. Every series needs exactly one point per label — a shorter one misaligns every value after the gap, and a chart that is subtly wrong still reads as authoritative, so the whole spec is dropped instead. A pie's slices are its labels, so it draws the first series only.

Theme the series with --ag-ui-chart-1 … --ag-ui-chart-6, size it with --ag-ui-chart-max-width, and style the block through the chart-block, chart-title and chart-legend parts.

A chart stops at its own width, and is sized in pixels rather than scaled to them. Two separate things, and a widened panel needs both.

It is drawn for the width the block actually has -- one SVG unit per CSS pixel -- and redrawn when that width changes, so a 10px axis label is 10px in a 380px panel and in a 1200px one. Where the labels no longer fit, the axis draws every second or third rather than a smear of overlapping words. Below 220px it goes back to scaling, since at that size nothing fits either way.

And it takes the width it needs rather than the width it is offered, capping at --ag-ui-chart-max-width (480px): widening the panel should no more resize a chart than it resizes a message. Raise the token for a bigger chart and the labels stay 10px -- the cap is about how much room the drawing gets, never about how big its type is. Height follows width inside a 160-320px band.

docs.title: Drawing something other than a chart
docs.text:
render_chart is built on a seam any tool can use. A ClientTool may declare a pure render beside its handler:

chat.registerTool({
  name: "show_route",
  description: "Draw the route on a map.",
  parameters: { type: "object", properties: { stops: { type: "array" } } },
  handler: () => "route shown",
  render: (args) => buildMapElement(args.stops),   // pure; no side effects
});

render is the only half a restored transcript replays. Replaying a tool's effect is out of the question — re-running a form-filling tool on every reload is a bug. The replay path is handed the render function alone, never the tool that owns it, so the code that runs on restore cannot reach handler even by mistake: adding a "no render? fall back to the handler" convenience there means changing a type signature first, which is the moment the question gets asked.

That is why render has to be a pure, deterministic function of its arguments — it runs again every time the conversation is restored.

docs.title: Drawing other things the server pushes
docs.text:
activityType is an open string the protocol does not enumerate — "chart" is just the one the component ships a renderer for. Register your own and the server can push anything it likes into the transcript:

chat.registerActivityRenderer({
  type: "build_status",
  render: (content) => {
    const el = document.createElement("div");
    el.className = "build";
    el.textContent = `Build ${content.status}`;
    return el;   // null: could not be drawn; an empty fragment: nothing to draw
  },
});

render runs again on every thread load, so it carries the same contract as a client tool's render: a pure function of content and the context it is drawn in (below), deterministic, and free of effects outside the node it returns. Activities are materialised into role: "activity" messages and persisted with the transcript, so a renderer that writes to the page instead of returning DOM fires again on every restore.

The component places what you return, keyed by the activity's messageId, so a server repeating an id replaces your node rather than adding a second one — the same in-place update charts get, unless render hands back the node it was given (below). Returning null removes whatever was there, with a console warning: live and reload should agree, and the stored content is the version that could not be drawn.

Content that is fine and has nothing to show — a record meant for the model, a list with nothing in it for the user — returns an empty DocumentFragment instead: nothing is drawn, nothing is logged, the type is not reported as unhandled, and anything drawn under that messageId before is taken away. A renderer that always returns one is how a type is known and deliberately drawn as nothing.

chart, compaction, suggestions and the types below are registrations exactly like yours, not privileged branches, so registering any of those names replaces the built-in, before or after the element connects.

docs.title: Built in: what pydantic-ai's AG-UI adapter sends
docs.text:
pydantic-ai's own AG-UI adapter sends activities of its own, and each has a built-in renderer, so none of them shows in unhandledActivityTypes.

activityType Drawn as pydantic_ai_enqueued_messages Each user message's text as a user bubble (message-user), as text and never as HTML, in an enqueued-messages column with an enqueued-messages-note caption (string enqueuedMessages). Messages the run took in while it was working, through RunContext.enqueue. Other roles draw nothing. mcp-apps A run notice (run-notice-mcp-app) that the app view cannot be shown here, naming its resourceUri (string mcpAppUnsupported, token {uri}). pydantic_ai_compaction, pydantic_ai_tool_availability_delta, pydantic_ai_model_settings_delta, pydantic_ai_capability_load_delta Nothing: records the adapter keeps for the model.

compaction, django-ag-ui's own notice, is separate and stays drawn. The adapter's enqueued messages are drawn only: @ag-ui/client does not send activities back to the server, so a later run does not see them as turns.

docs.title: Updating a surface in place, and drawing it inert on replay
docs.text:
render takes a second argument, an ActivityRenderContext: { messageId, previous, live }. A one-argument renderer ignores it and keeps working as before.

  • previous is the node your renderer returned for this messageId last (null on the first draw). Update it and return it, and the component leaves it where it is instead of replacing it, so a field the user is typing into keeps its value and its focus when the server redraws the activity. Returning a new node replaces the old one, as before.
  • live is true when the draw comes from the run in flight and false when a stored conversation is put back (a reload, a thread picked from the drawer, a Retry redrawing what came before it). A surface drawn with live: false must be inert: no button that acts, every input disabled. A restored surface is redrawn on every thread load, and acting on it would send an action from a turn the conversation has moved past.
chat.registerActivityRenderer({
  type: "approval_form",
  render: (content, { previous, live }) => {
    const form = previous ?? document.createElement("form");
    if (previous === null) {
      form.append(document.createElement("input"), document.createElement("button"));
      form.querySelector("button").textContent = "Approve";
      form.onsubmit = (event) => {
        event.preventDefault();
        void chat.run({ forwardedProps: { action: "approve", note: form.elements[0].value } });
      };
    }
    for (const control of form.elements) control.disabled = !live;
    return form;
  },
});

docs.title: Which carrier should the server use?
docs.text:
AG-UI leaves exactly two payload names open, and they are not interchangeable:

Carrier Reaches Persisted Replayed Content ACTIVITY_SNAPSHOT the transcript yes yes Imperative CUSTOM your page, as ag-ui-custom no no

⇒ Content has a place in the conversation and should come back. An imperative has no place and no meaning once acted on — replaying "refetch the board" on every thread load is a bug, not a feature. If it has to survive a reload, it is content.

docs.title: Finding out what arrived
docs.text:
An activity nobody registered for draws nothing and logs nothing — that is the protocol's own answer, and warning would fire on every forward-compatible server. But silence is hard to debug, so the names are readable:

chat.unhandledActivityTypes; // ["build_status", …]

Note "chart" appears there until you call enableCharts(["activity"]), which is the honest answer to "I pushed a chart and nothing happened".

docs.title: A2UI surfaces
docs.text:
An agent can describe a small interface as A2UI 1.0 components: a form, a choice, a card with a button. The ./a2ui entry draws it from the data the server pushes, never from markup, and sends what the user does back as a run.

import { registerA2ui } from "@artooi/agents-web-components/a2ui";

const chat = document.querySelector("ag-ui-chat");
registerA2ui(chat, {
  onError: (message) => console.warn(message), // the default
});

registerA2ui does three things:

  • registers the a2ui-surface activity renderer, the activity type @ag-ui/a2ui-middleware and django-ag-ui's render_a2ui tool send;
  • posts this renderer's catalog as a context entry on every run, under the description the server looks it up by, so the server offers the agent a render_a2ui tool for exactly these components. The catalog is a2ui/v1/catalog.json in this package, and its id is that file's URL;
  • starts a run for each action a surface sends, with the action in forwardedProps.a2uiAction and the user turn django-ag-ui stores for it, so the bubble drawn now is the one a reload shows.

It returns the function that stops posting the catalog.

The catalog is the A2UI basic catalog's twelve components (Text, Image, Icon, Row, Column, List, Card, Divider, Button, TextField, CheckBox, ChoicePicker) and fourteen functions (required, regex, length, numeric, email, formatString, formatNumber, formatCurrency, formatDate, pluralize, openUrl, and, or, not).

An Image loads only an http: or https: URL, an image data: URL, or a relative path on the page's own host; openUrl takes the same, minus data:. Anything else the agent names draws no image and opens nothing.

A surface restored from a stored conversation is drawn inert: its buttons do nothing and its inputs are disabled, because acting on it would send an action from a turn long past.

Errors go to the host. A2UI's error message (VALIDATION_FAILED, EXPRESSION_ERROR, EXECUTION_ERROR, INTEGRITY_ERROR) is meant for the agent, but neither @ag-ui/a2ui-middleware nor django-ag-ui carries one back yet. So a live surface hands each error, as the spec's {version: "1.0", error: {code, surfaceId, message, path?}}, to onError (by default console.warn) once per draw of the surface; a redraw with new content reports again. It draws a notice where it could not draw, and starts no run. A component or a catalog this renderer does not hold is drawn as an a2ui-notice.

docs.title: Vendoring it
docs.text: ./a2ui/bundle (dist/agents-web-components.a2ui.bundle.js) is the same entry as one file with everything inlined, to load beside the main bundle. It reaches the element only through the chat it is handed, so it carries none of it. It does carry its own copy of marked and DOMPurify, since Text draws markdown through the same sanitiser as the transcript.

docs.title: Styling a surface
docs.text:
Each surface is an a2ui-surface part; every component on it carries part="a2ui-<kebab-case type>" and data-a2ui-id, its id on the surface. The parts are a2ui-text, a2ui-image, a2ui-icon, a2ui-row, a2ui-column, a2ui-list, a2ui-card, a2ui-divider, a2ui-button, a2ui-text-field, a2ui-check-box and a2ui-choice-picker. A variant shows on the component as a data- attribute: data-variant on Text and Image, data-fit on Image, data-justify and data-align on Row and Column, data-align and data-direction on List, data-axis on Divider, and data-unknown on an Icon whose name has no glyph. A slot whose child has not arrived yet holds a hidden a2ui-placeholder. An @accessibility label or description lands on the component's native control where it has one (the <button>, the <input>), and on the component otherwise. Inside the inputs:

  • Button: a2ui-button-control, a2ui-button-message;
  • TextField: a2ui-text-field-label, a2ui-text-field-input, a2ui-text-field-message;
  • CheckBox: a2ui-check-box-label, a2ui-check-box-input, a2ui-check-box-text, a2ui-check-box-message;
  • ChoicePicker: a2ui-choice-picker-label, a2ui-choice-picker-filter, a2ui-choice-picker-options, a2ui-choice-picker-option, a2ui-choice-picker-input, a2ui-choice-picker-option-text, a2ui-choice-picker-message.

The surfaces read the element's theme tokens, so a theme set on <ag-ui-chat> reaches them.

docs.title: MCP Apps views
docs.text:
A tool on an MCP server can come with a view: an HTML resource the MCP Apps extension draws beside its result. The agent pushes an mcp-apps activity naming the view and its server; the ./mcp-apps entry frames the view and speaks the host's end of its bridge. Without it the element draws a notice that the view cannot be shown.

import { registerMcpApps } from "@artooi/agents-web-components/mcp-apps";

const chat = document.querySelector("ag-ui-chat");
registerMcpApps(chat, {
  url: "/agent/mcp-apps/", // the host's route
  sandboxProxyUrl: "https://sandbox.example.com/proxy.html", // optional, another origin
});

The route takes a JSON POST of { serverId, method, params }, sent through chat.request so it carries the element's headers and credentials, and answers as django-ag-ui's does: 200 with { "result": ... }, the MCP result object (a tool result with isError is still a result), or { "error": { "code", "message" } } with a JSON-RPC code for a call it cannot relay, which a view's tools/call is answered with as it is. Any other status or body fails the call with -32000. method is resources/read (the view's HTML, read once per server and URI for the page) or tools/call (a tool the view calls). A toolset with no id sends no serverId, and its views draw the notice.

The view is framed once it first scrolls into sight: in a srcdoc frame with sandbox="allow-scripts" and the view's CSP as the first <meta> of its head, or, with sandboxProxyUrl, in the proxy on its own origin. When the view leaves the document, in sight or not (a thread switch, a cleared conversation, or the chat itself removed), its frame and bridge go, and it is framed again if it returns. A srcdoc frame inherits the host page's CSP, so a host with a strict script-src sets a proxy.

The package ships a proxy page, @artooi/agents-web-components/mcp-apps/sandbox-proxy.html (dist/sandbox-proxy.html): one static file with its script inline. Serve it as is on a second origin, one the page's own origin is not, and name its URL as sandboxProxyUrl. It puts the view in an inner sandbox="allow-scripts" frame with the view's CSP as the first <meta> of its head, so serve it with no CSP header of its own (an inner srcdoc frame inherits one) and let the host page's frame-src reach that origin.

# The static site served at https://sandbox.example.com, not the chat's origin.
cp node_modules/@artooi/agents-web-components/dist/sandbox-proxy.html sandbox-site/proxy.html

registerMcpApps(chat, {
  url: "/agent/mcp-apps/",
  sandboxProxyUrl: "https://sandbox.example.com/proxy.html",
});

The bridge is JSON-RPC over postMessage (MCP Apps 2026-01-26), read only from the view's own frame:

The view sends The host ui/initialize answers with hostContext: theme, styles.variables, locale, displayMode (inline until it asks), availableDisplayModes (["inline", "fullscreen"] for a live view, ["inline"] for a stored one), containerDimensions (inline, the frame's width and a maxHeight of 640; fullscreen, its width and height) and platform: "web" ui/notifications/initialized sends ui/notifications/tool-input (the call's arguments), then ui/notifications/tool-result ui/notifications/size-changed sets the frame's height, at most 640px; the view scrolls past it tools/call once the user allows it (below), sends it to the route with the view's serverId and answers its result, or its error with the route's code; declined, -32000 "Tool call denied" ui/message once the user allows it (below), sends its text as the user's next message (chat.sendMessage); isError when nothing was sent; declined, -32000 "Message sending denied" ui/open-link opens an http(s) URL in a noopener tab; isError for any other ui/request-display-mode fullscreen fixes the view over the page in the same frame, which does not reload, with an exit control (string mcpAppExitFullscreen); Escape, that control or inline returns it to the transcript at its height. Answers the mode it is in after: the current one for pip, and for a stored or torn-down view ui/notifications/request-teardown sends ui/resource-teardown, then closes the view to the notice anything else answers -32601

tools/call, ui/message and ui/open-link are refused while the view is drawn from a stored conversation rather than a live run, and once it has asked to be torn down. Once initialised, the view is sent ui/notifications/host-context-changed with what changed when the theme attribute, the system scheme, the frame's width or its display mode does (displayMode and containerDimensions, however it was switched). Fullscreen shows the view's box as a manual popover, in the top layer, so it covers the viewport above the host page's own layers whatever --ag-ui-z-index is and in every placement; a browser without popover (Firefox before 125) draws it as a fixed box inside the host's stacking context instead. One view per registration is fullscreen at a time; a second's request returns the first inline.

A view never acts unseen. A view's script runs as soon as it is framed and can post at any moment, and the host cannot tell a click inside a cross-origin sandboxed frame from a script: user activation there is not visible to the page. So every tools/call and ui/message of a live view waits for the user in a confirmation card under the view's frame (pinned under it while fullscreen), which names the tool and its arguments, or shows the exact text to be sent. Confirm runs it; Cancel answers the view -32000. The card takes the confirmation card's styles and the confirm part (plus mcp-app-consent), its prompts are the strings mcpAppConfirmTool and mcpAppConfirmMessage, and it takes no focus, so a key meant for the composer cannot answer it. A view's requests are asked one card at a time, in order; a card still waiting when the view asks to be torn down, or leaves, is declined, and a request allowed after the view went stored or asked to be torn down is refused. There is no setting to turn it off. The MCP Apps specification allows exactly this: a host "MAY request user consent" for ui/message, and may subject other requests "to further user approval".

A view that navigates its own frame is closed to the notice: a srcdoc frame seen by the host, a proxied one reported by the shipped proxy page with ui/notifications/sandbox-view-navigated.

styles.variables are the element's own tokens, resolved in the scheme drawn now, under the MCP Apps names: --color-background-primary (--ag-ui-bg), --color-text-primary (--ag-ui-fg), --color-border-primary (--ag-ui-border), --font-sans (--ag-ui-font), --border-radius-md (--ag-ui-radius) and the shades between them, so a view themed from them follows the chat's theme.

docs.title: Run notices: compaction and agent skills
docs.text:
Some things a run does are neither text nor a tool the user asked for — the server condensed earlier turns to fit the context window, or the model pulled in an agent skill. Those render as run notices: a muted one-line annotation inline in the transcript, styleable via the run-notice, run-notice-icon and run-notice-text parts.

Two different things are called "skills". The prompt chips and slash palette below are a human affordance — prompts the user launches. An agent skill is a folder of instructions the model chooses to load mid-run. Only the second produces a run notice.

Neither notice needs configuration here — both appear when the server is set up to produce them.

Compaction. django-ag-ui emits a standard AG-UI ACTIVITY_SNAPSHOT with activityType: "compaction" when a compaction capability trimmed the history; the notice reports how many messages went. Server side, that means wrapping the capability in CompactionObserver — see django-ag-ui's compaction guide. Activity events of any other type pass through untouched, so another producer on that channel is not mistaken for a compaction.

Agent skills. There is no dedicated event for these: loading a deferred capability is an ordinary load_capability tool call, which is what reaches the client. The component recognises it, renders Using skill <id>, and suppresses the raw tool card that would otherwise appear beside it — on the live stream and on restored history alike, so a reload shows the same transcript. A load_capability call with no usable id falls back to a normal tool card rather than being dropped, since it is still real activity.

Both strings are overridable like every other — historyCompacted (token {count}) and usingSkill (token {name}).

docs.title: Skills: prompt chips and slash palette
docs.text:
Skills are pre-defined prompts the user can launch from a chip or the /-command palette. They are opt-in via two attributes:

<ag-ui-chat endpoint="/agent/" data-prompt-chips="true" data-slash-commands="true"></ag-ui-chat>

A Skill is { name, title, description?, prompt?, sendImmediately?, chip? }. Skills are merged from three sources — backend → embed → client (later wins by name):

  • data-skills-url — a JSON endpoint, fetched with the element's headers.
  • data-skills — an inline JSON catalog.
  • setSkills(skills) — set the client catalog from JS.
chat.setSkills([
  // Server-resolved: no prompt here, so picking it sends the bare "/triage"
  // token and the agent decides what it means.
  { name: "triage", title: "Triage this", chip: true },
  // Client-side: the page owns the wording and fills the placeholders.
  { name: "summarize", title: "Summarize page", prompt: "Summarize {title}.", chip: true },
]);

Prefer omitting prompt for anything internal. A skill is often where a project's workflow is written down most plainly, and a catalog is either a plain GET or sits in the page source — so shipping the wording to the browser publishes it. Without a prompt the component sends /name and the agent expands it (from the harness Skills capability, or your own instructions); the text never leaves the server. django-ag-ui's SkillRegistry supports this by leaving prompt unset.

A skill that does carry a prompt may use {placeholder} tokens; the skillContext property (() => Record<string, unknown>) supplies the values, filled in before send. A missing placeholder blocks the send and shows a hint instead.

chat.skillContext = () => ({ title: document.title });

Picking a skill sends it. A chip that needs a second click to do anything is a two-step shortcut. Set sendImmediately: false on a prompt-carrying skill to pre-fill the composer instead — useful when the user is expected to edit before sending. A server-resolved skill always sends.

docs.title: The skill editor
docs.text:
With django-ag-ui's stored skills (AGUIServer(skill_editor=True), 0.83.0 or later), the element can offer an editor for the skills the caller may write. Point data-skill-editor-url at the mount's skills/editor/ route:

<ag-ui-chat
  endpoint="/agent/"
  data-skills-url="/agent/skills/"
  data-skill-editor-url="/agent/skills/editor/"
  data-skill-editor-button
  data-slash-commands="true"
></ag-ui-chat>

The editor opens in place of the conversation, below the header, from a "Manage skills" row at the foot of the / palette (under data-slash-commands; alone under a bare / when nothing matches) and, with data-skill-editor-button, from a Skills button in the header (openSkillEditor() and closeSkillEditor() drive it from your own chrome). It lists the skills the server says the caller may write, off ones included, with "Turn on" on an off row; it creates, edits and turns skills off; and "Draft one with the agent" closes it and sends /create-skill, whose draft comes back as an approval card. History, Checkpoints and New chat close it first. The server keeps every rule: a refused save shows the server's message ({"error"}) under the field its "field" names (django-ag-ui 0.84.0 and later name the field: name, description, body, userInvocable, modelInvocable or enabled), and above the form when it names none.

docs.title: Whose skill it is
docs.text:
