docs.title: The conversation list in your own chrome
docs.text:
<ag-ui-threads> lists a chat's conversations where you put it: as rows in a rail, or as pills in a bar. It keeps nothing of its own. It reads the chat's conversationStore, marks the thread on screen as current, and drives the chat through the thread API.

<header>
  <ag-ui-threads for="chat" variant="pills"></ag-ui-threads>
</header>
<aside><ag-ui-threads for="chat"></ag-ui-threads></aside>
<ag-ui-chat id="chat" endpoint="/agent/"></ag-ui-chat>

<script type="module">
  import { defineChat } from "@artooi/agents-web-components/chat";
  import { defineThreads } from "@artooi/agents-web-components/threads";
  defineChat();
  defineThreads();
</script>
  • Binding. for names the chat's id, looked up in the list's own root, the document or the shadow root it sits in; a chat added later is picked up when it first reports its thread. Or set the chat property, which wins over for until it is set back to null. With neither, the list binds to the chat of an <ag-ui-agents> provider: the one its agents attribute names by id, else the nearest one around it, and lists again each time the provider moves its chat to another agent. for wins when both are present.
  • variant. list (the default) draws rows and an empty text. pills draws a strip that stays on one line and scrolls sideways, and no empty text. Both give each conversation a delete behind an inline confirm, which calls chat.deleteThread; in a pill the confirm opens on the pill's own line.
  • Picking a row fires ag-ui-threads-select (THREADS_SELECT_EVENT, detail { threadId }, bubbling, composed and cancelable), then calls chat.switchThread, which cancels a run in flight, as the built-in list does. Call preventDefault() to route to the conversation yourself; otherwise it is the moment to close a popover the list sits in.
  • Run marks. A row whose store reports thread status carries one mark: waiting, failed, running or unread, in that order of precedence, as data-status on the row and a dot with its word for a screen reader inside the row's button.
  • refresh() reads the store again. The list does so after every thread, title and run-finished event, and takes the rows of every ag-ui-threads-change; call it when something else changed the store, such as another tab. threads (read-only) is the rows on screen, as the store last listed them. A redraw keeps keyboard focus on the row, delete or confirm it was on.
  • strings translates every piece of text (label, untitled, empty, delete, deleteConfirm, deleteYes, deleteNo, and the marks' running, waiting, failed, unread), merged over the English, so { deleteNo: "Abbrechen" } changes that one string.
  • Styling. Parts list, row (plus row-active on the thread on screen), row-button, mark (plus mark-running, mark-waiting, mark-failed or mark-unread), delete, confirm, empty. The chat's colour tokens apply, plus --ag-ui-danger (the delete confirmation and the failed mark) and --ag-ui-waiting (the waiting mark). The list takes the light or dark half of each from the page's own color-scheme, since it sits in your chrome rather than in the chat's. The host carries data-empty when the chat has no conversations.

The main /bundle does not carry the element. Without a build step, load /threads/bundle beside it:

<script type="module">
  import { defineChat } from "./agents-web-components.bundle.js";
  import { defineThreads } from "./agents-web-components.threads.bundle.js";
  defineChat();
  defineThreads();
</script>

docs.title: Thread status
docs.text:
django-ag-ui 0.84.0, on a mount with a run store, lists each thread with its run's status (idle, running, waiting, failed), its last_read_at, a reason when it failed and, when it waits, AG-UI interrupts. RemoteConversationStore (what data-threads-url builds) reads them onto ThreadMeta as status, reason and interrupts, and works out unread. An older server, or a mount without a run store, lists none of them and nothing below happens.

  • Unread is a thread that changed after it was last read, by the server's clock on both sides, or was never read (last_read_at is null), and is not running now. The server keeps no mark until a thread is read once, so a thread a routine started shows as unread until it is opened, and so does every thread stored before the server kept read marks.
  • Read. When the element reads a thread (markRead), the store posts POST <threads-url><id>/read/, and only once a list carried status, since the route is mounted only beside a run store. The thread then reads as read here until it changes again. A read made before such a list is held and sent with the first one; a page reloaded before any list loses it, and the thread shows unread until opened again.
  • Keeping it fresh is the host's choice, and opt-in. data-thread-status="poll" asks the list again every five seconds with its ETag (a 304 costs nothing); "stream" follows the same URL as Server-Sent Events, read with fetch so the headers and cookie policy apply, reconnecting when the server ends it. A server that answers the stream request with JSON (a WSGI deployment) is polled instead. Without the attribute the list is read when it always was: when the drawer opens, a thread switches, or <ag-ui-threads> re-lists. Each list the watch receives is counted into the unread badge and fired as ag-ui-threads-change (THREADS_CHANGE_EVENT, detail { threads }), which <ag-ui-threads> draws. A store of your own takes part by implementing watchThreads(listener, transport).
  • A waiting approval is answered where it waits. Opening a thread whose run is parked on an approval (metadata.kind == "approval") shows the approval card on its tool call, as a live run's interrupt does, and the answer starts the run again with resume built by @ag-ui/client's buildResumeArray. Asked of the store when the thread is restored (waitingInterrupts(threadId), which data-threads-url answers from the list with its ETag), so it needs no data-thread-status. Stop, or leaving the thread, while the person decides sends and writes nothing: the run stays parked and is offered again next time. A question or external interrupt, or a mix, is marked waiting and not offered: the server maps every resume entry to an approval, so answering one that way would approve it. A host driving its own AgUiClient answers a parked run the same way with client.answerParked(interrupts), which asks its resolveInterrupts once and sends the resume.

docs.title: Tool-call display modes
docs.text:
How tool calls are drawn is set via the data-tool-display attribute (or toolDisplay property), one of grouped / inline / minimal / compact / full (default grouped; an absent or unknown value reads as grouped):

  • grouped — the default. A run's consecutive tool calls fold into one quiet row, "Worked through 5 steps", with a note such as "1 failed" beside it, and the calls one click down as full cards, or in the mode data-tool-group-display names. Anything else in the turn (text, a confirmation, a question) ends the group, and the next call starts a new one; a call's own rendered output does not. A group of one call shows that call's own label. See The step group.
  • inline — the lightest mode: a single status row (icon + summary, no card chrome) with the result behind its own toggle. Reads as one line of the answer — pairs with the answer well.
  • minimal — tool name + status pill only.
  • compact — name + status, with arguments and result behind a single collapsed toggle.
  • full — arguments visible, result behind the toggle. The default before grouped: set data-tool-display="full" to keep per-call cards.

Whichever mode is on, a settled card's body holds two labelled regions — Arguments and Result (or Error / Declined) — each with its own part and each pretty-printed. They are never run together into one block, so where the call ends and the answer begins is always visible. Style them via the tool-card-args / tool-card-result parts, their headings via tool-card-section-label, and the whole body via tool-card-body.

A card names its status as a part. ::part() takes no attribute selector, so a rule on tool-card-status reaches every outcome alike. The card and its status pill each carry a modifier beside the base part, one of pending, deferred, done, error, declined or interrupted, and it is replaced whenever the status changes:

ag-ui-chat::part(tool-card-error)        { border-color: crimson; }
ag-ui-chat::part(tool-card-status-error) { font-weight: 700; }

The attribute is live. Changing data-tool-display between the four card modes restyles every card already in the transcript, the way data-answer-well does — the modes are pure visibility over one DOM shape, selected by the shadow CSS from the host attribute. Grouping is decided as each card is built: switching to grouped folds only the calls drawn afterwards, and switching away from it flattens the groups already drawn, by CSS, into exactly the cards the new mode builds (the group stops generating a box and its row is hidden).

docs.title: Choosing how a group draws its calls
docs.text:
Under grouped, an opened group draws its calls as full cards unless the data-tool-group-display attribute (or toolGroupDisplay property) names another of the card modes: compact, minimal or inline. Each draws the regions the flat card of that mode draws, laid out as a row of the group's list rather than as a boxed card. An absent or unknown value reads as full, so nothing changes for a host that does not set it.

<ag-ui-chat endpoint="/agent/" data-tool-group-display="compact"></ag-ui-chat>

It is read only under grouped. Under one of the four card modes the groups are flattened into that mode's cards and the inner value is ignored; switching back to grouped applies it again. It is live like the outer attribute: changing it restyles groups already in the transcript.

A call waiting on an approval shows its arguments and its Approve and Deny buttons in every inner mode, as it does in every card mode, and Approve takes focus when the group opens for it.

docs.title: The step group
docs.text:
Under grouped the row reads, by state:

State (data-state on the tool-group part) Label Mark running "Working through 3 steps", and the running step's label as a note spinner waiting "3 steps", with "1 waiting for you" accent dot done "Worked through 3 steps" check error "Worked through 3 steps", with "1 failed" in the danger colour error mark

"N declined" is added as a note whenever a step was declined. While the group is folded, "N pre-approved" is added when a reviewer model or a routine approved calls in it with no one asked; opened, each of those cards says so itself and the row drops the count. data-count carries the number of steps and data-open whether the cards are showing; the head is a button with aria-expanded.

  • It opens itself while a step waits on you. A server-side approval renders inside the gated call's own card, so a folded group would hide the question it is asking: the group opens when a step goes deferred, once per wait, and stays folded if you fold it again. It opens before the approval is drawn, so the Approve button takes focus and scrolls into view. A client-side confirmation and an ask_user question render in the answer beside the group rather than inside a card, so they are in view without it opening; the row still reads waiting ("1 waiting for you") while one is open, as the card carries a data-asking flag for the group to read, and its data-status stays pending.
  • A one-step group is named after its call, and the card's head is not repeated inside. A turn with exactly one call reads as that call's label ("Fill field"), and the opened list shows the card without its own tool-card-head (the row's state mark and notes carry the status). The Details toggle and arguments stay, except under data-tool-group-display="minimal", where the card is only its head: there the row draws no chevron, though it still opens for an approval. A call that records a decision or a pre-approval keeps that one note from its head, and its row opens onto it with a chevron, under minimal and with no arguments or result too. A card display mode keeps the whole head. A run that grows to two calls brings both heads back.
  • A running sub-agent does not open it. The row keeps its spinner and names the delegation instead, "Delegated to researcher" (the subAgentDelegatedTo string).
  • Repeated labels are told apart. Two "Fill field" steps read "Fill field" and "Fill field (2)": the ordinal is an element of its own (part tool-card-repeat) beside the card's name, so tool-card-name is never rewritten, and a card mode hides the ordinal.
  • Rendered output stays in view. A tool's render output is placed after the group, in call order, rather than inside it, so a chart is never one click down. It does not end the group: a later call joins the group above it, which is also how a restored conversation draws the run.

Parts: tool-group (with the state beside it as tool-group-waiting, tool-group-running, tool-group-done or tool-group-error), tool-group-head (the button), tool-group-icon, tool-group-label, tool-group-meta (holding one .tool-group-note per note), tool-group-list (the cards), and tool-card-repeat on a repeated step. The focus ring is --ag-ui-ring and the disclosure chevron --ag-ui-ico-chevron. Strings (strings / data-strings): toolGroupSteps, toolGroupWorking, toolGroupWorked (each with {count}, always 2 or more), toolGroupWaiting, toolGroupFailed, toolGroupDeclined, toolGroupPreApproved (each with {count}) and toolStepRepeat (with {n}).

<!-- Keep per-call cards, as before grouped was the default -->
<ag-ui-chat endpoint="/agent/" data-tool-display="full"></ag-ui-chat>

docs.title: Drawing a card's body yourself
docs.text:
A thirty-field result is a wall of JSON where a host wanted a table, or a sentence. formatToolPayload is the seam: it is asked about each region of each card and may return a Node to take it over, a string to replace its text, or null to leave the built-in pretty-print alone.

chat.formatToolPayload = (payload) => {
  if (payload.kind !== "result" || payload.toolName !== "list_orders") {
    return null; // everything else keeps the default rendering
  }
  const table = document.createElement("table");
  // ... build it from JSON.parse(payload.text)
  return table;
};

Both halves come through the same hook, told apart by kind: arguments carries the parsed record the call was made with, result the raw string the tool returned plus the outcome it settled on. A region a formatter took over is marked data-formatted, which relaxes the preformatted whitespace the default JSON block relies on — a table would otherwise inherit it as mangled cell spacing. Whitespace only: the card's face, frame and scroll cap stay, so one long payload still cannot stretch the transcript, and a host wanting different typography restyles the tool-card-result part.

This is presentation, not translation. The card and the model already read separate copies of a tool result — the model's is maintained by @ag-ui/client from the same event — so a formatter changes what the person reads and nothing the agent reads. That is what makes restyling safe here, and it is also why rewording belongs on the server: renamed there, the new wording reaches the model's prose too, instead of leaving the card disagreeing with the answer beside it. A returned string is set as text, never parsed as markup — this is not a second HTML channel into the transcript.

A gated call carries the decision (approved by you / declined by you, part tool-card-decision, attribute data-decision) — from the client-side confirmation card and from the server-side approval interrupt alike. The prompt itself disappears once answered: a prompt and a record are different objects, and the record is the card.

The annotation is session-scoped, like the "run interrupted" notice. AG-UI carries no approval message — the answer rides resume[] as transient run input — so a reload restores the tool call and its result but not the note that a human waved it through. If you need "who approved what" durably, that is an audit concern rather than a transcript one; record it server-side.

A call no person was asked about can still have been approved: by a reviewer model, or by a routine's standing grant. No interrupt is raised for it, so the tool call card carries the mark. When a result's metadata.answered_by (django-ag-ui 0.81.0 or later stamps it, live and on the stored tool message) starts reviewer: or routine:, the card gets data-answered-by="reviewer" or "routine" and a note in its head (part tool-card-answered-by, strings answeredByReviewer / answeredByRoutine). Any other value, and a result without the key, render exactly as before. Unlike the decision, the mark survives a reload, because it is read off the stored message. It is display only: the server's audit record is the authority.

If a tool's schema carries an x-summary string (use X_SUMMARY_KEY), the card shows it on the label instead of the raw tool name.

Every card leads with a status icon drawn entirely in CSS — a spinning ring while the call runs, then a check / cross / slash / dotted ring on success / error / decline / not finished. Re-theme it via custom properties (or the tool-card-icon part): --ag-ui-tool-icon-done, --ag-ui-tool-icon-error, --ag-ui-tool-icon-declined, --ag-ui-tool-icon-interrupted (quoted-string glyphs) and --ag-ui-tool-spin-duration (spinner speed; the spin respects prefers-reduced-motion).

<ag-ui-chat endpoint="/agent/" data-tool-display="compact"></ag-ui-chat>

docs.title: Delegated sub-agents
docs.text:
A run that hands work to a sub-agent reads as a stall. The parent's delegate_task card sits at "running…" for the child's entire duration — however many tools the child calls, however long it takes — with nothing on screen to say anything is happening.

If your server narrates that, the component draws it. The wire is an ordinary AG-UI CUSTOM event named ag_ui.subagent, carrying:

Key Meaning delegationId the parent's own delegate_task tool-call id — not the child's run id agent the child agent's name phase one of started, tool_call, tool_result, finished, failed, or a task phase status a pre-rendered line, ready to show tool toolCallId, name and ok, on the two tool phases only task the task a task phase names, on those phases only

Exactly one started opens a delegation and exactly one finished or failed closes it. ok is a tri-state: null while the child's call runs, true on a result it accepted, false on one that came back to it.

Because the key is the parent's call id, the surface attaches to a card that already exists rather than floating a second element with the same identity: one collapsed row per delegation, live, carrying the server's status line and nothing else, expanding onto the child's own tool calls. A ten-step child costs one row until somebody opens it, and there is no second visual language — it reads the way tool cards already read.

status is why the collapsed row needs no wording of its own. The structured keys are there for a host that would rather write its own.

The row shows in every display mode, including minimal. It sits outside the card body rather than in it, because the body is what the density modes hide — and a live progress line that only appeared in full would leave exactly the stall it exists to end. Same reasoning that shows a deferred card's arguments whatever the mode.

A failure carries no exception text on this channel, deliberately — the same reasoning that redacts a RUN_ERROR, since an exception's words are written for an operator. The detail rides the ordinary tool result for that delegation, which lands in the same card's Result region a few pixels below. Nothing here invents words the server declined to send.

None of it is persisted. A CUSTOM event never enters the message list, so nothing replays on a thread restore — which is the right half of the carrier split: a delegation that was live an hour ago is not live now, and replaying its progress would be a lie about a run that is over. Reload mid-run and the tool card is still there; the nested detail is not. That is the intended behaviour.

A child's tool calls on the protocol's own events stay the child's. A server may also send them as TOOL_CALL_* events tagged with the delegation's subagentRunId, as django-ag-ui does from 0.90.0. The component draws no card of the parent's for a tagged call and never runs it, even when a frontend tool has the same name; the row above still follows the CUSTOM steps. @ag-ui/client keeps those calls in the message list under the same tag. A restored thread skips them, and a child's call left without a result is never answered for the parent.

Like ag_ui.invalidate, this name is routed rather than forwarded: it draws itself and does not also arrive as an ag-ui-custom event. Every other name still reaches your page untouched.

Style it through tool-card-subagent (the region inside the card), subagent, subagent-row, subagent-icon, subagent-status, subagent-steps, subagent-step, subagent-step-icon and subagent-step-name. The two glyph states reuse the card's own --ag-ui-tool-icon-done / --ag-ui-tool-icon-error properties and its spinner speed, so re-theming the cards re-themes these. The row's own chrome comes from subAgentWorking and subAgentSteps in UiStrings; everything else on the row is the server's text.

docs.title: Task control
docs.text:
Under django-ag-ui's task control (0.90.0+, SubAgents(task_control=TaskControl())) a delegation is a task the parent's model manages, and the row draws what happens to it. The task's moments arrive on the same ag_ui.subagent event with tool: null, a server status line and a task record:

phase When task carries backgrounded the task moved to the background taskId, reason (requested, auto, question) steered the task was sent a message taskId, message, source question the task asked the parent a question taskId, questionId, question answered the question was answered taskId, questionId, answer, source cancel_requested the task was asked to stop taskId, forced, source retried a remote task's worker is running it again taskId, attempt

From django-ag-ui 0.91.0 the steps carry what was said, cut at 8000 characters with truncated beside it, and source says who acted: user for the controls below, model for the run itself. The row shows the server's status line ("researcher: steered by you"); the open question's text is drawn beside the Answer control, so only where the controls are. The panel's data-phase is the latest moment. What outlasts a moment is stamped on the subagent part for a host to style:

Attribute Set data-task-id the task the steps name data-background once the task left the foreground; the value is the server's reason data-awaiting-answer from question until answered, or until the task settles data-cancel requested or forced, once a cancellation was asked for data-attempt a remote task's retry count, on retried data-source user or model: who acted on the latest steer, answer or cancel data-answerable the open question's id, only while the controls are live and Answer is offered

A task closes on the protocol's events as before, and two SUBAGENT_ERROR codes are not the child failing: code: "cancelled" settles the row as data-phase="cancelled" ("researcher was cancelled", subAgentCancelled), and code: "unfinished", sent when the run ends while a background task is still open, as data-phase="unfinished" (subAgentUnfinished). Any other code, or none, is failed, on the server's words. A resumed task opens a new delegation, with a fresh subagentRunId, on the delegate_task call that resumed it, so it draws on that call's card. None of it is stored, as above: a restored thread shows the cards and no task progress.

The glyph follows: a cancelled task draws the card's --ag-ui-tool-icon-declined and an unfinished one its --ag-ui-tool-icon-interrupted, both muted, and an open question stops the spinner for a still ring in the accent colour.

docs.title: Steer, answer and cancel
docs.text:
With data-threads-url set, a live task's row offers three controls beside it, in the subagent-controls part:

  • Steer opens a field (subagent-reply) whose text is sent to the task.
  • Answer appears while the task waits on a question, beside the question's text (subagent-question), and sends the answer to that question.
  • Cancel asks the task to stop before its next model request. Once that request is on the stream (data-cancel="requested") the button reads Stop now and stops the task at once.

Each control is one POST to the route django-ag-ui (0.91.0, with a run_store) serves beside the thread, with the element's headers and cookie policy:

Control Route Body Steer <threads-url><thread>/tasks/<taskId>/steer/ {"message"} Answer <threads-url><thread>/tasks/<taskId>/answer/ {"question_id", "answer"} Cancel <threads-url><thread>/tasks/<taskId>/cancel/ {"force"}

The server acknowledges with 202, and the row does not change until the step for the act arrives on the stream: a control never sets a state itself. A request is sent once and never retried, a 401 included, since a steer sent twice is two messages. A refusal is worded from its reason code under the controls (subagent-control-error): not_running, no_task and no_run as subAgentControlFinished, not_waiting as subAgentControlNotWaiting, not_live_here, remote and a server without the routes as subAgentControlUnavailable, and anything else as subAgentControlFailed. The controls are withdrawn when the task settles.

Under the default grouped tool display the controls sit inside the group's folded row: a background task's delegating call settles as soon as the task goes to the background, so the row reads done. Steer and Cancel are one click down. When the task asks a question, the group opens itself, once for each question, so Answer and the question's text are in view; if the user folds it again it stays folded until a new question arrives. A question with no question id, or one shown with no live controls (no data-threads-url), does not open it.

The parts are subagent-controls (the region), subagent-question, subagent-actions (the three buttons' row), subagent-steer, subagent-answer, subagent-cancel, subagent-reply, subagent-reply-input, subagent-reply-send and subagent-control-error. Their text comes from subAgentControls (the group's label), subAgentSteer, subAgentAnswer, subAgentCancelTask, subAgentForceCancel, subAgentSend, subAgentSteerPlaceholder and subAgentAnswerPlaceholder. The routes reach only a run live in the process serving the request and only top-level tasks; anything else is refused and worded as above.

docs.title: Child sessions
docs.text:
A child session (django-spec-agents' start_session) runs headless in a thread of its own and sends nothing into the parent's stream. What persists is its receipt, the call's tool result ({ agent_id, thread_id, run_id, note }), so the link is read from that, on the live result and on a restore alike: the card that started a child links to the child's thread, and still does after a reload. A refusal, or any other result, draws no link.

  • A child that needs you. When the thread list the chat holds (the drawer's listing, or data-thread-status's watch) shows the child's row waiting, the link reads childSessionNeedsYou ("The researcher task needs you") instead of childSessionOpen, and carries data-status. It still only opens the child: the parent never draws the child's approval or any control that answers it.
  • The breadcrumb. When the thread on screen is a child (django-ag-ui 0.86.0 lists parent on its row, read onto ThreadMeta.parent), a line between the header and the transcript reads parentThread ("From {title}"), or parentThreadUnlisted when the list does not hold the parent, and opens it.
  • The drawer nests each child under its parent's row (drawer-row-child, inside a drawer-children group), in the parent's date group whatever the child's own date. A child whose parent is not listed, or that a filter matched without its parent, stands at the top level.
  • A child's report and question. When a child's report wakes its parent, django-spec-agents 0.28.0 and django-ag-ui 0.91.0 mark what no user wrote with metadata.origin. The wake's own line (wake) is not drawn. A report (task_output) is drawn as a card titled childReport ("Report from helper") holding the plain task.body, never the <task_output> frame the model saw, and a question (task_question) as one titled childQuestion ("Question from helper"). The card's link reads childSessionOpen and opens task.threadId the way the card link does. Both arrive inside the run's enqueued-messages activity live, and as marked user messages in server-held history; each draws the same. A failed report carries data-outcome="failed"; style both through child-report and child-report-link.

Opening a thread asks first. A link, a report's link or the breadcrumb dispatches ag-ui-open-thread (OPEN_THREAD_EVENT, detail { agentId, threadId }, typed OpenThreadDetail), bubbling, composed and cancelable. agentId is the receipt's agent_id, or the parent's store scope (null when unscoped). The chat cannot tell which agent it serves, so unless a listener calls preventDefault() it then opens the thread in place, as a drawer pick does, letting go of a run in flight. A host whose child runs on another agent's mount takes the event, opens that thread where it lives, and prevents the default (under an <ag-ui-agents> provider that is done for a listed agent):

chat.addEventListener("ag-ui-open-thread", (event) => {
  if (event.detail.agentId !== null && event.detail.agentId !== "assistant") {
    event.preventDefault();
    openAgentThread(event.detail.agentId, event.detail.threadId);
  }
});

Nothing to opt into. The breadcrumb and the needs-you wording wait for a list: after a reload straight onto a child under a remote store, that is the first drawer open, switch or data-thread-status tick.

docs.title: Editing a gated call before approving it
docs.text:
AG-UI's resume payload carries editedArgs, and the protocol gates it on the agent's own approveWithEdits capability. The approval card can offer it:

chat.approveWithEdits = true; // your server accepts editedArgs

Off by default, and an assertion about your server rather than a negotiation — capabilities are not on the wire this component reads, so it cannot check. Turned on against a server that ignores editedArgs, a user would edit arguments it silently discards, which is worse than not offering.

The card then shows the call's arguments as editable JSON. editedArgs rides the resume payload only when something actually changed, so a server can tell "approved as proposed" from "approved, but like this" without diffing what it already sent. Unparseable JSON, or JSON that is not an object, keeps the card open with the reason on it rather than approving the original behind the user's back.

Only offered for an interrupt naming a tool call this component holds a card for — the card is where the arguments still are.

docs.title: File uploads
docs.text: Set data-attachments-url (django-ag-ui's AttachmentsView) to let the user attach files to a message. A button, drag-and-drop, and paste appear on the composer; each picked file uploads out-of-band (multipart, with the element's headers) and shows a chip in a pending tray — uploading (with a progress bar) → ready, or error with a retry. On send, the ready files' refs ride on the user bubble as read-only chips and the agent reads their contents server-side via the read_attachment tool. The wire stays vanilla AG-UI: only lightweight refs ({ id, name, mime, size }) travel, never the bytes, in the user message's metadata under attachments — the one place on a message @ag-ui/client 1.0 does not strip an unknown key from. django-ag-ui reads them from there as of 0.63.0; an older one reads only the top-level key 1.0 removes, so against it the agent is never told a file was attached.

docs.title: Pasting
docs.text:
A paste carrying files puts them on the tray, the same way the picker and a drop do — a screenshot straight from the clipboard, or a file copied in the file manager.

Two rules keep it from stealing a paste that was never about files. Text pastes carry no files at all, so ordinary pasting is untouched. And the default is prevented only when the clipboard carries no text: copying a rich selection that happens to contain an image puts both on the clipboard, and swallowing the words someone meant to paste in order to attach a picture they did not is the worse of the two failures.

A pasted blob that arrives with no filename — some engines hand one over that way — is given one, rather than reaching the server as an empty filename and showing in the tray as a chip with no label.

<ag-ui-chat
  endpoint="/agent/"
  data-attachments-url="/agent/attachments/"
  data-attachment-accept="image/*,application/pdf,text/plain"
  data-attachment-max-bytes="10485760"
></ag-ui-chat>

Client-side accept / size checks are an instant-feedback nicety — the server is authoritative. Refs persist on the message, so a restored conversation re-renders its chips. Without the attribute the affordance stays hidden and the chat is text-only.

The built-in handler sends the element's headers / getHeaders with every upload, and honours credentials="include" — with the caveat that it is an XMLHttpRequest (for real progress events), whose cookie switch is two-state: include turns it on, every other value leaves it off. See Authenticating requests.

Swapping the upload transport. The built-in multipart POST is just the default uploadHandler. Set your own to use a different transport — a resumable tus-js-client adapter, direct-to-S3 multipart, etc. — without touching the tray, the chips, or the AG-UI wire (refs are transport-agnostic). The handler is (file, onProgress) => Promise<AttachmentRef>; when set, the affordance appears even with no data-attachments-url, and your handler owns its own endpoint and headers:

import { Upload } from "tus-js-client";

chat.uploadHandler = (file, onProgress) =>
  new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const up = new Upload(file, {
      endpoint: "/tus/",
      headers: chat.headers,
      onProgress: (sent, total) => onProgress(sent / total),
      onError: reject,
      onSuccess: () =>
        resolve({ id: up.url.split("/").pop(), name: file.name, mime: file.type, size: file.size }),
    });
    up.start();
  });

The server side is the matching half: the agent reads bytes by ref id, so point the read_attachment store at wherever your transport persisted them (django-ag-ui's AttachmentStore is the seam). The refs themselves never change shape.
